message.content: Lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (family Equidae, order Perissodactyla) diverged very early in mammalian evolution. Their most recent common ancestor was a small, early placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago—an ancestor of the group that eventually split into the lineages that became modern carnivores and the odd‑toed ungulates (horses, rhinos, tapirs, etc.).
